newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close up, October at new high. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close up, October at new high. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]

text.p: Strong cash market kept CME live cattle futures supported and prices ended mostly higher with October setting a new contract high for the third consecutive day.
October set a new high of 73.200 cents per lb before closing at 73.175, up 0.450 cent on the day. Other months ended 0.100 cent higher to unchanged.

October showed further commercial demand and mixed short covering propted by the strong tone to cash beef and fed cattle markets. Packers paid up another $1 per cwt today to $72 (corrects from $73) and kept the trend moving upward, they said.
"Live is the drive here and that activity at $73 is what kept futures strong," said Joe Kropf from Joe Kropf and Sid Love Consulting.

Analysts said some packers had to cut back on kill rates recently due to the tight supply of market ready cattle. The reduced kill rate, along with continued good domestic and export demand for beef proded packers to pay the highest prices for fed cattle since March 8, 1995.
Kropf also noted that although boxed beef values were a little lower this monring, trade remained good and this should keep packer interest for fed cattle strong.
"Packer margins are a little better than they hoped for this week and beef has moved well," Kropf said.

Heavyweight choice boxed beef values had risen nearly $4.50 since the beginning of the month to $105.79 per cwt Wednesday, the highest level since December 1, before showing some price weakness Thursday morning.

Cargill Investor Services, E.D.&F. Man and LFG notably bought after R.J. O'Brien and local spreaders sold October early. Refco did fund rolling late, buying December and selling October, commonly know as the "Goldman roll", pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commercials hedged by spreading 64 puts/68 calls in February and 64 puts/70 calls in April, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle slipped at the close following higher corn futures, but underlying support continued from the strong tone to fed cattle and cash feeder markets, traders said.
"Feedlots have pen space and they are wanting feeders," Kropf said.
Feeder cattle closed 0.100 cent lower to 0.300 higher with October off 0.050 at 64.275 cents.
